title: Introduction to Programming for the Brain and Cognitive Sciences

sections.note: By the end of the course, students will have developed a piece of software of their choice (e.g., a simple experiment, video game, etc.). Core topics include program design, data wrangling and visualization, reproducible workflows (version control, environments), experiment/game scripting, statistical modeling, and simple machine-learning pipelines. Prior coding experience not required; familiarity with quantitative research methods recommended. RESTRICTED CLASS: Restricted to BCOG majors until Thursday, Nov. 19 at approx. 9:00 A.M.

Same as PSYC 492. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours. Prerequisite: Senior standing in Psychology, consent of instructor, and students must arrange to do a research project with a faculty member.
